quickAnswer: Start your Asian-side walk at Kadıköy Ferry Pier around 10:30, tasting regional Anatolian dishes and market staples inside Kadıköy Çarşı before looping north into Yeldeğirmeni's mural-covered streets. Finish south along Moda Sahili for sunset over the Marmara Sea, then walk 15 minutes back to Kadıköy Pier for frequent Şehir Hatları ferries to Karaköy or Beşiktaş.
category: Inner Pages — 20 Istanbul Micro-Districts & Landmark Guides

body.text: What food stops make Kadıköy Çarşı Istanbul's best daytime culinary walk?

Kadıköy Çarşı packs fishmongers, pickle bars, spice merchants, Anatolian lokantas, and specialty coffee roasters into five pedestrianized blocks just inland from the ferry docks. Unlike tourist-heavy Old City streets, residents do their daily grocery shopping here, keeping turnover high and ingredient quality consistently sharp from late morning through early evening.

Anchor lunch on Güneşlibahçe Sokak at [Çiya Sofrası](https://roamistanbul.com/neighbourhoods/kad-koy/), known for rotating regional stews, stuffed vegetables, and dishes from southeastern Anatolia alongside its two neighboring kebab and lahmacun kitchens. Round out your grazing loop with seasonal fish sandwiches (balık ekmek), aged Kars cheeses, and raw Anatolian honey highlighted in [Go Türkiye's Istanbul Street Food guide](https://goturkiye.com/istanbul/street-food), plus house-brined turşu (pickles) and roasted coffee near the Armenian Surp Takavor Church. Save room for a filter pour-over on Muvakkıthane Street at [Montag Coffee Kadıköy](https://roamistanbul.com/neighbourhoods/kad-koy/) before heading uphill.
How do you loop through Yeldeğirmeni's murals and indie cafes?

From Kadıköy Ferry Pier or the market edge, walk eight minutes northeast toward Haydarpaşa to enter Yeldeğirmeni (Rasimpaşa). Late-nineteenth-century apartment blocks—originally built for German railway engineers—serve as multi-story canvases for international street murals, interspersed with bakeries, design studios, and neighborhood cafés along Karakolhane Caddesi and Duatepe Sokak.

A compact 60-to-75-minute loop covers Yeldeğirmeni without backtracking. Enter via Karakolhane Caddesi, turn onto Duatepe Sokak and Recaizade Sokak to spot large-scale wall paintings profiled in local neighborhood guides such as [Roam Istanbul's Kadıköy directory](https://roamistanbul.com/neighbourhoods/kad-koy/), and pause at Yeldeğirmeni Sanat, a restored historic French church converted into a municipal concert and exhibition hall. Because sidewalks are narrow and gently sloped, late morning or early afternoon offers the clearest light for photographing building facades without parked delivery vans blocking lower panels.
Where do locals watch sunset along Moda Sahili?

After looping back through Bahariye Caddesi—following the nostalgic T3 tram tracks past the Kadıköy Bull statue—head south to Moda Sahili, the grassy coastal promenade curving below Moda Caddesi. Locals gather along the stepped stone seawall, around the wooden Moda Pier (Moda İskelesi), and at the cliffside tea gardens overlooking the Princes' Islands and the Old City silhouette.

body.text: Arrive at the promenade 30 to 40 minutes before sunset on clear weekends, as the concrete steps and grassy lawns fill rapidly with friends sharing tea, simit, and cold drinks. If you prefer seated table service over the seawall, the historic tea gardens above the bluff—Moda Aile Çay Bahçesi and Bomonti Çay Bahçesi—offer shaded benches facing west.
Which ferry pier takes you back to Karaköy or Beşiktaş?

Return to the main Kadıköy Ferry Pier (Kadıköy İskelesi) on Rıhtım Caddesi, where separate clearly marked terminals serve the [Şehir Hatları Kadıköy–Karaköy–Eminönü line](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/en/timetables/domestic-trips/inner-istanbul-ferry-lines/kadikoy-karakoy-eminonu-163) and the direct Kadıköy–Beşiktaş crossing. Both municipal routes run roughly every 15 to 20 minutes into the late evening and take 20 to 25 minutes across the Bosphorus mouth.

Check the electronic overhead departure boards or the [Şehir Hatları Domestic Trips schedule](https://sehirhatlari.istanbul/en/timetables/domestic-trips) before tapping your Istanbulkart, as the Karaköy/Eminönü terminal sits slightly west of the Beşiktaş terminal along the waterfront promenade. While waiting for a boat, you can browse the second-floor municipal bookstore [İstanbul Kitapçısı Kadıköy](https://roamistanbul.com/neighbourhoods/kad-koy/) or grab a quick coffee at Beltur Kadıköy İskele Kafe inside the pier building.

items: Carry a loaded Istanbulkart (or contactless bank card where accepted) for ferries and the T3 nostalgic tram.
Wear cushioned walking shoes; the full Çarşı–Yeldeğirmeni–Moda–Pier circuit covers roughly 6 to 7 kilometers on cobblestones and paved paths.
Keep small Turkish lira bills on hand for market pickle cups, street simit, and cash-preferred tea gardens.
Time Çiya Sofrası slightly early (11:45–12:15) to get seated immediately while the full daily pot-dish selection is fresh.
Bring a light windbreaker for the open upper ferry deck after sunset, even on warm afternoons.

faq.q: How long does the full Kadıköy, Yeldeğirmeni, and Moda walk take?
faq.a: Allow 5 to 6 relaxed hours, including a sit-down lunch in Kadıköy Çarşı, a 75-minute street-art loop in Yeldeğirmeni, coffee in Moda, and sunset on the coastal promenade.

faq.q: Is Kadıköy Çarşı open on Sundays?
faq.a: Most restaurants, cafés, bakeries, and many market stalls stay open on Sundays, though a few specialty wholesale counters and smaller family-run shops close or open later.

faq.q: Can I take the nostalgic T3 tram instead of walking back from Moda?
faq.a: Yes. The circular T3 tram loops from Kadıköy Pier up Bahariye Caddesi, around Moda Caddesi, and back down to the ferry docks, saving uphill walking if your legs are tired.

faq.q: Are there direct ferries from Moda Pier to Karaköy or Beşiktaş?
faq.a: Standard commuter crossings to Karaköy, Eminönü, and Beşiktaş depart from the main Kadıköy Pier rather than Moda Pier. Walk 15 to 20 minutes north along the waterfront or ride the T3 tram to reach the main docks.

faq.q: What is the best day of the week to visit Kadıköy and Moda?
faq.a: Tuesday through Thursday deliver lively market energy without the dense Saturday and Sunday sidewalk crowds along Moda Sahili and Bahariye Caddesi.

faq.q: Can I connect this walk with the Marmaray train instead of a ferry?
faq.a: Yes. Ayrılık Çeşmesi (one stop from Kadıköy on the M4 metro, or a 12-minute walk from Yeldeğirmeni) connects directly to the cross-Bosphorus Marmaray line to Sirkeci and Yenikapı.
